subproblems.title: A unit-scale blow-up η_{−v,1#} is the translation by v
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), v ∈ ℝ^P and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n). Then there is a test form ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with ω'(y) = ω(v + y) for every y ∈ ℝ^P such that currentEval(blowUp S (−v) 1, ω) = S(ω'). Here blowUp S (−v) 1 = η_{−v,1#}S ∈ 𝒟_n(η_{−v,1}(ℝ^P)) is the push-forward of S by the dilation η_{−v,1}(y) = −(1⁻¹·(−v)) + 1⁻¹·y = v + y (contract blowUp: restrictDomain followed by affinePushforward with linear part dilationCLM P 1 and translation −(1⁻¹•(−v))), and currentEval T φ is T(φ) when φ is a test form with tsupport φ inside the domain of T, and 0 otherwise.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (v : Euclid P) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), ∃ ω' : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, (∀ y, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (v + y)) ∧ currentEval (blowUp S (-v) 1 one_ne_zero) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = S ω'
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 1 of the parent proof (Reduction): Simon 6.2.23 for the proper affine diffeomorphism η_{−v,1}(y) = v + y, i.e. the translation τ_v of Simon Lemma 7.3.5 (chapter-07.txt lines 386–395). It uses only the contract definitions dilation, dilationCLM, blowUp, currentEval and the SimonGMT definitions GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain (restrictDomain_apply), GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward (affinePushforward_apply), affinePullbackTestOn and affinePullbackForm (x ↦ (ω(b + L x)).compContinuousLinearMap L). It is the translation counterpart of the accepted Submission.dtc_cwv_isConeCurrent_of_pullback_invariant (which unfolds blowUp C 0 λ).

1. (The translate is a test form.) Put ω'(y) := ω(v + y). ω is C^∞ with compact support (IsTestForm). The map y ↦ v + y is affine, hence C^∞, so ω' = ω ∘ (v + ·) is C^∞. The map y ↦ v + y is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P (Homeomorph.addLeft v, inverse z ↦ z − v), so tsupport ω' = (tsupport ω) − v is the image of a compact set under a continuous map, hence compact (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph). Trivially tsupport ω' ⊆ univ. So ω' ∈ TestFormOn univ n, and ω'(y) = ω(v + y) holds for every y by definition.
2. (The dilation is the translation.) dilationCLM P 1 = 1⁻¹ • id = id and −(1⁻¹ • (−v)) = v, so dilation (−v) 1 (y) = v + y for every y. Hence dilation (−v) 1 '' univ = univ: every x ∈ ℝ^P equals dilation (−v) 1 (x − v).
3. (currentEval takes its test-form branch.) ω is a test form and tsupport ω ⊆ univ = dilation (−v) 1 '' univ by step 2, so by the definition of currentEval, currentEval(blowUp S (−v) 1, ω) = (blowUp S (−v) 1)(⟨ω, _⟩), the value of blowUp S (−v) 1 ∈ 𝒟_n(dilation (−v) 1 '' univ) on ω regarded as an element of its test-form space.
4. (Unfolding blowUp.) By definition blowUp S (−v) 1 = (S.restrictDomain h).affinePushforward L b _ with L = dilationCLM P 1 and b = −(1⁻¹ • (−v)), where S.restrictDomain h is S restricted to W = (y ↦ b + L y)⁻¹'(dilation (−v) 1 '' univ) ⊆ univ. By affinePushforward_apply, the definition of affinePullbackTestOn, and restrictDomain_apply (the inclusion testFormOnInclusion does not change the underlying form), (blowUp S (−v) 1)(⟨ω, _⟩) = S(ω''), where ω'' ∈ TestFormOn univ n has underlying form affinePullbackForm L b ω, i.e. ω''(y)(w_1, …, w_n) = ω(b + L y)(L w_1, …, L w_n).
5. (Identification.) By step 2, b + L y = v + y and L w_i = w_i, so ω''(y)(w) = ω(v + y)(w) = ω'(y)(w) for all y ∈ ℝ^P and all w ∈ (ℝ^P)^n (ext). Hence ω'' and ω' have the same underlying form, and as elements of the subtype TestFormOn univ n they are equal (Subtype.ext). Therefore currentEval(blowUp S (−v) 1, ω) = S(ω'') = S(ω'), which together with step 1 proves the claim for this ω'. ∎

```lean
    ω.property.1.1.comp (contDiff_const.add contDiff_id)
  have hcs : HasCompactSupport (fun y => (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (v + y)) :=
    ω.property.1.2.comp_homeomorph (Homeomorph.addLeft v)
  let ω' : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n :=
    ⟨fun y => (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (v + y), ⟨hsm, hcs⟩, subset_univ _⟩
  refine ⟨ω', fun y => rfl, ?_⟩
  -- `η_{−v,1}(ℝᴾ) = ℝᴾ`, so `currentEval` takes its test-form branch
  have hV : dilation (-v) (1 : ℝ) '' univ = univ := by
    refine eq_univ_of_forall fun x => ⟨x - v, mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    simp [dilation, dilationCLM]
  have h : IsTestForm (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ∧
      tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ dilation (-v) (1 : ℝ) '' univ :=

  rw [currentEval, dite_eq_left h]
  -- unfolding `blowUp`: the affine pullback of `ω` by `y ↦ v + 1⁻¹ y` is `ω'`
  change S _ = S ω'
  congr 1
  apply Subtype.ext
  funext y
  ext w
  change (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (-((1 : ℝ)⁻¹ • -v) + dilationCLM P 1 y)
```

subproblems.title: v ∧ ξ = 0 almost everywhere when the fixed vector v is tangent almost everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(U, n) (M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient), μ := R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M, and v ∈ ℝ^P. Suppose that for μ-a.e. x the orthogonal projection of v onto approxTangentPlane n M x (the approximate tangent plane T_xM, defined as ⊥ when none exists) equals v. Then for μ-a.e. x and every (n+1)-covector β on ℝ^P, ξ(x)(β.curryLeft v) = 0, where (β.curryLeft v)(w_1, …, w_n) = β(v, w_1, …, w_n).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (v : Euclid P), (∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection v = v) → ∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1), R.orient x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β v) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 2 of the parent proof (v ∧ ξ = 0): the translation analogue of 'x ∈ T_x spt C for μ_C-a.e. x, so in particular x ∧ C⃗ = 0' in Simon's proof of 7.3.1 (chapter-07.txt lines 355–358). It is the argument of the accepted Submission.dtc_cone_wedge_vanishes with the point x replaced by the fixed vector v.

1. (Orientation holds μ-a.e.) The field R.orients says: for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. Since μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ is absolutely continuous with respect to Hⁿ⌞M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), this also holds μ-a.e. Intersecting with the hypothesis, it suffices to fix x such that (a) p_{T_x}(v) = v, where T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x, and (b) there are Q as above and an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) with span(range τ) = Q and either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for every n-covector α or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for every n-covector α; and to fix an (n+1)-covector β.
2. (T_x = Q.) Since some Q' satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q' (namely Q), approxTangentPlane n M x is, by its definition, the subspace chosen by Classical.choose from this existence statement; approximate tangent spaces are unique (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so T_x = Q.
3. (v ∈ Q.) By (a) and step 2, p_Q(v) = v, hence v ∈ Q (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff).
4. (y ↦ β(y, τ) vanishes on Q.) Put λ(y) := (β.curryLeft y)(τ) = β(y, τ_1, …, τ_n). It is linear in y (curryLeft is linear). For each j, λ(τ_j) = β(τ_j, τ_1, …, τ_n) = 0, because the entries in positions 0 and j + 1 coincide and β is alternating (map_eq_zero_of_eq). By span induction (λ(0) = 0, λ(y + z) = λ(y) + λ(z), λ(a·y) = a·λ(y)), λ vanishes on span(range τ) = Q.
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 3 and 4, (β.curryLeft v)(τ) = λ(v) = 0. In the first sign case ξ(x)(β.curryLeft v) = (β.curryLeft v)(τ) = 0; in the second, ξ(x)(β.curryLeft v) = −(β.curryLeft v)(τ) = −0 = 0. ∎

```lean
/-- `v ∧ ξ(x) = 0` a.e. when `v` lies in the approximate tangent plane a.e. (the translation part of
the proof of Simon Lemma 7.3.5): `ξ(x) = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ` for an orthonormal basis `τ` of `TₓM`, and
`y ↦ β(y, τ₁, …, τₙ)` is linear and vanishes on each `τᵢ` (repeated entry), hence on `TₓM ∋ v`. -/
theorem Submission.dimred_cs_ti_wedge_vanishes : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (v : Euclid P), (∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection v = v) → ∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1), R.orient x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β v) = 0 := by
  intro P n U R v hproj
  filter_upwards [hproj, (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous _ _).ae_le R.orients]
    with x hx hor β
  obtain ⟨Q, hQ, τ, -, hspan, hξ⟩ := hor
  have hT : approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x = Q := by
    have h : ∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n R.carrier x Q := ⟨Q, hQ⟩
    rw [approxTangentPlane, dite_eq_left h]
    exact h.choose_spec.unique hQ
  have hvQ : v ∈ Q := hT ▸ Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff.mp hx
  have hβ : ∀ y ∈ Q, ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β y τ = 0 := by
    intro y hy
    rw [← hspan] at hy
    induction hy using Submodule.span_induction with
    | mem y hy =>
      obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := hy
      rw [ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply]
      exact β.map_eq_zero_of_eq _ (i := 0) (j := b.succ) (by simp) (Fin.succ_ne_zero b).symm
    | zero => simp
    | add y z _ _ hy hz =>
      rw [map_add, ContinuousAlternatingMap.add_apply, hy, hz, add_zero]
    | smul a y _ hy =>
      rw [map_smul, ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply, hy, smul_zero]
  rcases hξ with hξ | hξ
  · rw [hξ, hβ v hvQ]
  · rw [hξ, hβ v hvQ, neg_zero]
```
proof_key_steps: Transfer R.orients from Hⁿ⌞M to μ = θHⁿ⌞M (absolute continuity) and intersect with the tangency hypothesis.
approxTangentPlane n M x = Q by uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, so p_Q(v) = v gives v ∈ Q = span τ.
y ↦ β(y, τ_1, …, τ_n) is linear and vanishes on each τ_j (repeated entry), hence on Q ∋ v; so ξ(x)(β.curryLeft v) = ±β(v, τ) = 0.

subproblems.title: Cartan's formula for a constant vector field: d(ι_v β) + ι_v dβ = Dβ[v]
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let β be an (m+1)-form on ℝ^P (DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1), a map from ℝ^P to continuous alternating (m+1)-linear forms), let v, y ∈ ℝ^P, and suppose β is Fréchet differentiable at y. Let ι_vβ be the m-form z ↦ β(z).curryLeft v, where (β(z).curryLeft v)(w_1, …, w_m) = β(z)(v, w_1, …, w_m). Then, with d the exterior derivative (exteriorDerivative = Mathlib extDeriv) and Dβ(y) = fderiv ℝ β y, d(ι_vβ)(y) + (dβ(y)).curryLeft v = Dβ(y)[v].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (v y : Euclid P), DifferentiableAt ℝ β y → exteriorDerivative (fun z => ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft (β z) v) y + ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft (exteriorDerivative β y) v = fderiv ℝ β y v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 4 of the parent proof (Cartan's formula for a constant field), the infinitesimal form of Simon's homotopy formula Ch. 6, 2.25–2.26 (chapter-06.txt lines 441–458) for h(t, x) = x + tv. It is the constant-field counterpart of the accepted Submission.dtc_cone_euler_cartan. Convention (Mathlib extDeriv, alternatizeUncurryFin_apply): dω(y) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dω(y)), i.e. dω(y)(w_0, …, w_k) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i Dω(y)[w_i](w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_k). Write B := Dβ(y), a continuous linear map from ℝ^P to (m+1)-covectors.

1. (Derivative of ι_vβ.) Let Φ(α) := α.curryLeft v for (m+1)-covectors α. Φ is continuous linear (the linear isometry curryLeftLI followed by evaluation at v). Then ι_vβ = Φ ∘ β, so by the chain rule ι_vβ is differentiable at y with D(ι_vβ)(y) = Φ ∘ B, i.e. D(ι_vβ)(y)[u] = (B u).curryLeft v. In particular d(ι_vβ)(y) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Φ ∘ B).
2. (First term.) For w = (w_0, …, w_m) ∈ (ℝ^P)^{m+1}, by the formula for d and step 1, d(ι_vβ)(y)(w) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i ((B w_i).curryLeft v)(w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_m) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i (B w_i)(v, w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_m).
3. (Second term.) (dβ(y)).curryLeft v (w) = dβ(y)(u) with u = (u_0, …, u_{m+1}) := (v, w_0, …, w_m). By the formula for d, dβ(y)(u) = Σ_{j=0}^{m+1} (−1)^j (B u_j)(u_0, …, û_j, …, u_{m+1}). The term j = 0 is (B v)(w_0, …, w_m). For j = i + 1 (i = 0, …, m): u_{i+1} = w_i, removing entry i + 1 of (v, w_0, …, w_m) leaves (v, w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_m) (Fin.removeNth at a successor index commutes with Matrix.vecCons), and (−1)^{i+1} = −(−1)^i. Hence (dβ(y)).curryLeft v (w) = (B v)(w) − Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i (B w_i)(v, w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_m).
4. (Cancellation.) Adding steps 2 and 3, the two sums cancel term by term, so [d(ι_vβ)(y) + (dβ(y)).curryLeft v](w) = (B v)(w) = Dβ(y)[v](w).
5. Since w was arbitrary, the two (m+1)-covectors are equal (ext). ∎

subproblems.title: An action annihilating all v-directional derivatives is invariant under translation by v
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) and v ∈ ℝ^P. Assume R.action(γ) = 0 for all test forms β, γ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) with γ(y) = Dβ(y)[v] (fderiv ℝ β y v) for every y. Then R.action(y ↦ ω(v + y)) = R.action(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P).

It uses the sibling translate_derivative.

1. (Translates are test forms.) For t ∈ ℝ put β_t(y) := ω(tv + y). ω is C^∞ and y ↦ tv + y is C^∞, so β_t is C^∞; y ↦ tv + y is a homeomorphism (Homeomorph.addLeft (tv)), so β_t has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph). Thus β_t ∈ TestFormOn univ n.
2. (Derivative of a translate.) For every y, Dβ_t(y) = Dω(tv + y): the derivative of z ↦ ω(a + z) at y is Dω(a + y) (Mathlib fderiv_comp_add_left, a = tv).
3. (γ_t is a test form.) Put γ_t(y) := Dω(tv + y)[v]. Dω is C^∞ because ω is, so y ↦ Dω(tv + y) is C^∞, and applying it to the constant vector v gives a C^∞ map (ContDiff.clm_apply). Dω has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv), hence so does y ↦ Dω(tv + y) (comp_homeomorph); and Dω(tv + y) = 0 forces γ_t(y) = 0, so support(γ_t) ⊆ support(y ↦ Dω(tv + y)) and γ_t has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono). Thus γ_t ∈ TestFormOn univ n.
4. (Annihilation.) By step 2, γ_t(y) = Dω(tv + y)[v] = Dβ_t(y)[v] for every y, so the hypothesis with β = β_t and γ = γ_t gives R.action(γ_t) = 0, i.e. R.action(y ↦ Dω(tv + y)[v]) = 0.
5. (Zero derivative.) Let G(s) := R.action(y ↦ ω(sv + y)). By the sibling translate_derivative, G has derivative R.action(y ↦ Dω(tv + y)[v]) at t, which is 0 by step 4. As t was arbitrary, G is differentiable on ℝ with derivative 0 everywhere.
6. (Constancy.) A function ℝ → ℝ that is differentiable everywhere with zero derivative is constant (Mathlib is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero, a consequence of the mean value theorem); hence G(1) = G(0).
7. (Conclusion.) G(1) = R.action(y ↦ ω(1·v + y)) = R.action(y ↦ ω(v + y)) (one_smul), and G(0) = R.action(y ↦ ω(0·v + y)) = R.action(y ↦ ω(y)) = R.action(ω) (zero_smul, zero_add). Therefore R.action(y ↦ ω(v + y)) = R.action(ω). ∎
